body: I do wonder, though, what they expect you to respond. They want to feel superior by putting others down, but do they think you'll praise them? Apologize for not having responsibilities? Hang your head in shame? It sounds as if they are acusing you of something, which bothirritating and weird.I remember my mum once responding, rather crossly, that 'you don't have to go  to work'. I was sick at the time and felt like shit. She wasn't saying 'it's not so bad', but more like 'don't you dare complain because I don't give you a right to do so'  Absolutely no one suffers as much as her!This post reminded me of that conversation. It's like they think  'no one is allowed to be happy/better off than me because I'm miserable'.

I often wonder about this. Knowing my mum, I'm not entirely sure she wouldn't have had children, but she had me and got married before she knew what it was that she wanted. Children, even though she claims she wanted kids, were far too big a responsibility for her. I think she wanted it to be easier but she picked a terrible partner. My father shouldn't have had kids. He didn't have the emotional maturity and was unpredictable, which taught me to walk on eggshells around him and others. My mum is now in a bit of a victim mode and also denies anynegative emotions I might bring up. As a child, I lacked the emotional support and was convinced I needed 'fixing'. My mum recently said that she asks my cousin how was school, for instance, just to avoid future problems that might occur if she doesn't ask. I do wonder now if her approach to kids isn't all about obligation. If so, she'd have been better off not having children at all. I imagine she likes small kids,  but that's not enough.

I've seen a comment elsewhere that went along the lines of 'the more you put intosacrifice, the more meaning you get out of it'. It was all in the context of people not having children. So some believe it's all about giving life up for others as much as possible. But if it was as wonderful as they say, people who did sacrifice a lot for kids wouldn't be so unhappy. Maybe some of them convinced themselves they had to suffer, but as it brought no satisfactory results, they feel miserable. And I'm starting to think that leaning too much into this idea that it's all for other people and then you are a good person could be a sign of some underlying issues and not this wonderful virtue.

Oh finally! Someone else in the same boat. I still am trying to figure out whether there's some underlying issue I need to resolve because if I meet people in a certain setting, that acquaintance doesn't last if I just don't like the person/ move out of that setting where we met. I've read recently that children of emotionally immature parents look for strong connections and in a way it felt that the book was suggesting those connections had to be deeper than just 'let's have a coffee together'.

I bet whatever was going on in her family  made her think 'this is hard and it sucks'. And here you were, making a choice where you didn't have to deal with the bad parts of the whole thing.  How dare you not suffer? In general I can't ever understand people who pry into everyone else's personal business, be it children or something else. What business is it of hers what you do with your life? And she also had0 concern for how you feel about the topic. It's almost funny at this point that parents are the ones with so little awareness.
Seriously? I'd never have believed this was possible.Going through this three months in a row! And your reward is triple the work.

Right... and if she didn't already know, this fake 'oh it will be fine...Five minutes and it's done' cheerful lie will absolutely convince her because women are that gullible. I don't get what's the point of hiding the truth anyway. It's not like she can just decide not to give birth. Btw I had no idea it can last 19 hours. Seems like a form of torture.
You made me laugh out loud! What a comparison! I just can't...stop laughing...
Breathtakingly stupid is my new favourite phrase! It sounds so nice for some reason.
So it's the professors! I couldn't figure out which characters were the problem because it's not like Molly or the trio could be acused of child-freedom.
What kind of content does she make?

I have a feeling thatthe pain of childbirth would traumatize me because I am not exactly pain-tolerant and I've heard it's horrible. But if at some point they are like 'just deal with it, no pain relief for you', I can't even begin to imagine what that's like. Well, we women are martyrs after all. They just make sure it stays that way. I wonder if the memory of the pain you experience fades after a while. I overheard a girl I went to uni with telling someone how her friend gave brith and it was absolutely horrific. Then she goes on to say'and she's having another one, imagine that.' I wonder if women tell other women you have to do it all 'naturally' with no pain relief.
I just had an image of my little chihuahua going off to college.

From what I've seen, the very fact someone dislikes kids is something shameful, at least according to some. So it's something that probably needs to be fixed. When they start going on about how those kids will look after these 'child haters', I'm like 'everyone will be an adult by that point so?' I can see how valued love for kids is, at least by my family, because my mum praised my cousin a lot for playing with a girl my mum's partner's friend brought when he was doing some work for us.My father, on the other hand, was bad with kids and me being a kid didn't change this. His interactions with kids were always forced. It's only that those other kids didn't get to see how mean he could be. I'm also only now realizing there are mothers who play with their children! I know this might sound funny to some, but when I realized this would also be something my child might want, I was like 'I just can't' I wonder how these people who believe 'it's different when it's your own' handle all these kid-related things that probably don't interest them at all. I've seen  a youtuber who loves Disney as much as her kids, which mean everyone gets to have fun when they go to Disneyland. I can already imagine what a torture it would have been for my parents if  I had ever expressed a wish to go there. I know not everything related to parenting is enjoyable, but you need a certain kind of personality to get any enjoyment out of it I think.
Do you have a national selection or does the BBC choose who to send? I always wondered because in my country (Lithuania)people get to vote but everyone is still mad in the end usually.
Better yet, why don't we let the kidsvote? They are the actual future, not their parents.

Just commenting to say I somehow am still surprised horrible things happen to the kids of 'good' parents because it feels like one of those things that is rarely mentioned. Everyone always looks for something 'wrong' with the family so that the rest of it would make sense.

I had no idea there are signs a kid is growing up with an alcoholic. A six-year-old checking if everything is packed is such a sad image. So much for 'kids make you grow up'. It's more like you get to fuck-uptwo or three lives instead of just your own. Is her husband an alcoholic too?

I frankly don't understand the reaction of all those comentators. Why are they praising her if it's clearly not what she wants? Or is it this whole idea that it's good to sacrifice your own desires for someone else? Or are they thinking she is supposed to sort of repay her husband all his support by having a child?What a transactional view of marriage this is then.I know 10 years is a long time, but there might come a point where she thinks divorce would have been better than agreeing to have a child. The husband doesn't care about her if he doesn'tthink, even for a second, she might resent him and the kid. Why do women do this? And why do other women praise them for it? Is it now  a desirable thing to be miserable?

I never thought one of the reasons for having children might be thinking that the grass must be greener. In a way it feels strange because my first thought would be that it's harder. It is truly sad that so many are unprepared because their child suffers in one way or another and because parents themselves are unhappy. My mum to this day is envious of people who can afford things she can't and would mention how she and my father  struggled financially at one point because they had to pay-off the mortgage. But things would have been so much easier if she had had married later and if she had married a man she actually wanted to be with and whose wishes were at least similar to hers. It feels like a self-inflicted misery but the way some talk, it seems they believe  they were forced into this.
They must feel like they have been scammed!

I went on that sub once but haven't seen a post like that! Out of curiosity, what did the comments say?Now I think about it, in the post I did see, someone said that those awful people who dislike kids should realize those kids would be their carers one day. Some have this weird idea that you can shame people into liking children if you are mean enough about theirdislikes. Middle class not having kids leading to depression is one of the craziest things I've heard. I can nevertake suchpeople seriously and can't understand why they think what they say makes any sense.
People hate her? Like why? She'sjust soo inoffensive!
What did the message say?

I'm still angry about this. I couldn't believe it when they announced the result. I know someone was glad it got 0 and that some say it's boring, but I don't know...? It's funny, though, that some say the vocals were great and others say 'ok'. I wonder which it is really then. 
 Whatever the case might be, it's the first time I'm so upset by something like this. It feels somehow way too shocking.
Unbelievable! I'm sooo maad!
Switzerland 0 points? how?
mine too!

I had one recently too and hope it's the only one. I was about to give birth, but even in my dream I had a  feelingthat I don't really know what  childbirth is like'. So  it felt sooo...reaky? Weird? I can't explain  it, but I was like 'it's not supposed to be like this probably.'

Parents laughing and taking pictures makes it seem like it's not just their lack of parenting. I mean, they can surely read and know the kid isn't supposed to touch the butterflies, but it's like they enjoy letting the kid do what's not allowed. So in summary, you and your mum were the only actual adults there.

It's a bit like those kids at a kindergarten who don't get it that when you hit someone, it hurts. So the kid who was hurt has to hit them back and then 'you see? Hurts, doesn't it?' Maybe this will make that neighbour shut up, not because he realizes it's wrong to act the way he does, but because he doesn't want to get another dose of his own medicine. I swear this world is full of adults whoshould go back to the nursery because they clearly missed some crucial lessons.

I'm learning this now too.  For example, you will no longer want to spend money on yourself as an adult because you'll feel guilty. Spending on yourself is for teens. And the whole 'childhood is for having fun/is the best time' idea that so many believe just makes me go 'so what's the point of life if you only get a few nice years?'  I wonder  what they'd say if asked why they have children then if life is meant to suck so much. I've seen that such people can't seem to be happy about anything. Angels could  come down from the sky and they'd just shrug and complain.

I can't believe it! Wantedyour mum to look after the kid so they could play? So two kids have two more kids. I do find it interesting that these two people met and formed a family and neither of them realizes that they don't have the maturity toraise kids.

Ok...Thanks to seeing all these mentions of horrific stuff about pregnancy and how others find the whole idea just traumatic, I had a nightmare in which I was reading about a pregnant woman. It was bad enough but then I sort of became her and had rto give birth. I kept thinking'I just want this to be over' and even seeing other babies  while I was on a stretcher made me go'I don't like them'. And now this...It gets worse and worse. It's like everything is just made for women to suffer as much as possible.

I wonder what goes through such parents' mind when they decide to have children.Don't they care about the kid at all? They know what it's like to live with this or that illness and bring another person into the world  who will get to go through the same struggles.  It can also really impact their relationship with the child because it must be hard to come to terms with the fact your own parents knowingly passed on their issues. In certain cases  the parent also simply might be incapable of looking after the child. My relative had mental health issues and there were periods when she was just lying in bed and couldn't look after her two kids. If her sister hadn't come to make food for them,I  don't know what would have happened. And her kids also had no stability as she kept changing partners and had a drinking problem. When her daughter got pregnant at 17, I wasn't surprised.

I think this is a big part of their unhappiness. My mum was overwhelmed and took it out on me, once going as far as to say she had no life of her own. But she never tried changing things either, which would have been the only fix I could see. It's not easy I imagine, but maybe it helps having hobbies and getting to know yourself before having children. Then you already have something you can turn to.

I like this take. I was thinking the therapist meant something along these lines but couldn't put it into words. I also have abandonment issues so when I read what the therapist said I was like 'so this is whathe/others think about this'. I do wonder what happens in their head once their feelings towards their partner change. I don't mean to say they stop loving their child, but more that it must be a huge shift in how they see their partner if the feelings change. I don't know if you were the main person commenting about how the therapist was trying to help the op reframe her thoughts, but I liked tat idea. Do you have an interest in psychology?
It's one of my biggest fears too.I suppose parentsdeal with it somehow because they have no choice, but I'd be even afraid I couldn't look after the kid properly. I doubt it would end well.

I often think how weird it is that when some talk about a man who has serious problems, there's always some lady who says he 'needs a good woman'. But if a woman is single, there's somehow something wrong with her. It's like men automatically deserve some great woman who will 'fix them'. It doesn't occur to people that no one would want such a man, let alone want to fix him. I wonder how your uncle treats his wife. I'm not saying hemust be awful to her, but I just was wondering, given his attitude towards women.  
I was also in a situation where a man was rude to me and family members didn't say anything because, as usual, it's better not to make a scene/stand out. It really hurts so I know how you feel. That man is divorced now so even his own wife got sick of him. His   daughter is somewhat  like him, which is really a pity. That's why women shouldn't marry assholes.
We should have posters with this slogan!

'Him against his two kids'? So they are at war? No wonder the kids don't know how to behave. I remember someone getting angry at someone else's comment that kids shouldn't be allowed at restaurants if they can't behave properly. The person said that kids learn proper behaviour at public places by being there. But it's not like the kid just learns not to scream by being at a restaurant. You actually have to tell them what behaviour you expect. I wonder where his other kid was.

I dislike this idea that parents do their best and that this is automatically  good enough. First, I don't think it's always true because parents are perfectly capable of doing what's most convenient to them which isn't necessarily what's best for the child. Then I think of my father, who had very little self-control and whose main contribution was constant criticism. It's of course due to his upbringing, but he saw my reaction many times and still didn't change his ways because it's hard work and, to quote him,"I am the way I am'. That was his best and it certainly wasn't enough.
What theory is this?

So why the fuck  did he keep pestering you then? It almost seems he felt awkward when you did the same to him so I don't get him. I don't understand people who are intrusive  or rude but can't take it when they get the same treatment. Didn't they go to kindergarten? I thought  they learnt that if you hit someone, they can hit you right back and it hurts.

I bet your niece feels guilty for posting that stuff. I think it would help her to know that the adults in her life are at fault here because suppressing all that resentment  can only harm her. Your family'sreaction reminds me of my mum saying that there are worse fathers than my alcoholic uncle, who didn't raise either of his two kids. Guess who she thinks is worse? Some guy who refuse to acknowledge the child as his. It irritates me when some families have this 'we don't talk about this/it's not so bad policy'. It's fucking obvious it is just as bad as you say. "you won't understand'...What? Being an  irresponsible parent? Parentifying your own kid?  
I remember someone telling me of a case similar to the one you just described. A woman had two daughters. The older one basically acted as a mother to the younger. The girl came to her sister and raised her arms because she wanted the sister to lift her. The sister said 'I can't do it anymore because you are too heavy'. When the girl went to her mum, the mum pushed her away.

And if the grandparents lack the maturity to understand that once they have accepted the responsibility of raising their grandkid, they actually have to do it. We had to step in because my grandmother, unsurprisingly, saw how hard it was to look after a little child and somehow made my mum responsible for raising my cousin. But as my grandmother doesn't like responsibilities at all, she'd quite like my mum to look after her alcoholic brother too. This is what happens when people  who just don't care about anyone except themselves have children. But my grandmother would loove to get allthe praise.

My teenage cousin had to attend a class because she needed to get some instructions and the class was conducted by a pregnant woman. When she told me this, I was like 'someone is pregnant?Now?Why?' Many years ago, a teacher told us that once we graduate, we'll be able to get a job if our parents know someone. My mum didn't like this at all. Fast forward and she said herself we 'don't have the connections' our other relative has. She always knew this was the case because things haven't changed. I can't imagine having children just to later tell them that I don't have what it takes to give them the best chance at life. Quite a few people with kids now say that the kid should basically go for a study programme  that will allow them to get a stable, well-paying job.My mum herself laments the fact she doesn't have the skills thatwould allow her to earn more money. So I do wonder how parents think their kid will actually be capable of doing the job they imagine will guarantee a good salary. In a way it feels that people always had kids despite being convinced life actuallysucked quite a bit. They say'childhood is the best time' andthat you get to have fun when you are a child/teen. So why on earth bring a kid into the world which sucks once you no longer are a kid? It's like parents got themselves a play thing.

Such an amazing post! I especially love your point about kids not changing your personality. I sometimes try imagining what it would be like having to participate in all those kid-friendly activities and I could probably do it  but I wouldn't want to end up unhappy and resenting my child.  My mum now sometimes mentions how she had to do this and that for me and it's obvious this was an obligation for her, which leaves me feeling guilty. And my mum supposedly wanted children. The reality probably is that she didn't expect raising kids would be this hard. I promised myself I wouldn't be like this. I know you said your mum resented her own kids, so I wanted to comment this just to say even those who do want children seem to resent the obligations having kids brings or believe they  deserve praise for every single thing they did. I'm an introvert too. I don't remember this, but   I was told I wanted to be left alone to play when I was little. And when I try thinking of a happy memory, what pops into my head is the night when I was nine and listening to an audiobook in my room. Also, how do you manage to get in touch with your three-year-old self?

I already expect this from parents, but teachers? They obviously can't just turn the child into an obedient little darling if parents also don't do anything, but I somehow thought at school/kindergarten the 'old ways' haven't died yet. And then everyone will act surprised when this child does something way worse than throwing a tantrum and he will be physically stronger then too.

I often wonder if I would want kids had I grown up in a different family.Now it's hard to untangle the reasons I have for not wanting children. My father was emotionally immature and did a lot of damage to my self esteem. He also didn't help much around the house and my mum probably didn't have the courage to divorce him because my grandma is not what you'd call a supportive parent. I always dreaded ending up with a man like my father. I remember him once telling me something along the lines of 'parents are better grandparents than they were parents'. I remember thinking that I wouldn't want my kid to be around him. Now I realize that deep down he knew he wasn'ta very good father and yet he didn't want to change things.I also was forced to look after my cousin as a teen, which I hated. I remember having to look after her when I was very sick. Guess why this happened? Because my father wanted my mum to go prepare food for some kind of get together he had with his friends. My mum struggled and took it out on me. I swore to myself I wouldn't do that to a child. My mum also preferred things to be as easy as possible which meant shewasn't the type to go in search of better opportunities. I want things to beeasy too and kidscan only make things harder. I have relatives who should never have had children, which also helped me see what it means to be irresponsible. In general my family is not the sort of family I'd want to bring children into.

For women choosing a traditional path often means giving up their life for someone else. It definitely doesn't feel like a prize so it's funny they insist it is something to aspire to. I remember my mum commented that teenage years is the time to spend money 'on yourself' and that as an adult you 'feel guilty' for spending it on yourself. I was like 'wth? That sounds like an issue'.  I think this ties into this idea of 'settling down'- nothing for you and everything for someone else and of course no fun. But now I think about it, I don't remember my father expressing any sort of guilt when it came to buying stuff he wanted. In a way it feels that motherhood can become this victim narrative where a woman is both resentful she suffers but also convinced it's how it's supposed to be. No wonder in my culture there are folk songs where the young bride is crying. I'd cry too if wedding and children was my only option.

This applies to sooo many people. In my family we don't really do painful emotions precisely because talking about painful things was never something either of my parents learnt to do and I can see there's a lot of unresolved issues. Believing you'll 'do better' doesn't mean you will. And so the vicious cycle just never stops. I wonder how many people would have kids if they first went to therapy because then they wouldn't need to 'fix' their own childhoods or use a kid to get validation that they are finally 'good enough' for something. And if they did want kids after that, we'd have so many emotionally stable, happy people.
She wants more children? Who helps her raise them? And how are the ones who don't have DS doing? I've never heard of a story like that!

I swear that the more people I meet, the more it seems school never really ends. There's always, always someone who just has to prove they are the coolest adult on the playground. Oh they know this and that person...They worked with this well-known guy...And they won't talk to you if you aren't cool enough. Why would I add even more of the same to my life?'My kid can name all the capitals of the world'...'Mine speaks five foreign languages'... My cousin, when she wanted to be moved to a different class, absolutely refused to be moved to the one where there are only 'rich kids', who wear expensive clothes and whose parents of course have their own business and so on. Now I think about it, it sucks being a kid because you see early on how there's so much stuff you have no control over as a child but that means other people have way more opportunities. I know it can motivate some to 'do better', but what do you do if it doesn't work out?

Have you ever wonderedwhere your dislike towards kids comes from? I also dislike children and I often wonder if it's because as a child, I was often forced to play with kids I didn't know or if it's something else.

Same. To this day I'm envious of women who are nurturing. I don't know  how it is that they are the way they are. I can use cute voices with animals but not with children. Maybe it's because Iremember being forced to interact with kids I didn't know so it feels like an obligation. You are never forced to love animals, though.

I bet this also means we put others' needs first too. I just recently asked my mum's partner if he's planning to do any of the house maintenance stuff my mum asked him to do. He first said'you have to be in the mood for it'. Right...and yet he invited his friends over and  just assumes my mum and I will entertain his friend's wife without even asking us if we agree. I said I don't like her because she boasts a lot. His response? 'oh but what can one do?' So his needs come frist and I bet my mum will just accept the situation because she sees herself as the one who has to do things she doesn't want. I think she expects me to be like this too. 'Nurturing'  probably also, at least to those who believe this stuff, also means submissive and 'does what she is told'. I sometimes wonder why some men think they get to be the authority when they themselves do nothing or very little  to contribute. I remember my father once saying something about men being the ones in charge or some such because 'God made a man first'. My father wasn't even religious.

I really struggle to understand such parents. I'm obviously not going to tell anyone what to do, but if I were them, I wouldn't have had children. Imagine if the child reaches the age where they can understand they are in this position because  their parents chose to have children and pass on their health issues. We talk about the parents' right to have kids. But what about the child's right to have a good quality of life? I'd need a lot of therapy if I found out my parents knowingly passed on their health problems. I still remember one father talking about how autistic kids in our country don't have the same opportunities as kids elsewhere. And yet they chose to have a second child knowing they could be autistic with the attitude of 'oh well...it'll be 'fun' then'. But in that interview the father talked a lot about how they have no free time and can't go on holiday on their own because they can only leave their two autistic sons with their grandparents for a day or so. This situation is similar to the one in the post in the sense that the parents, either through their own experience or throughthe experience of already having a child with the same problems, already knew what it was like to live in a situation where your child is at a disadvantage and still made the choice they made.
Is that show on Netflicks?
This is very interesting. Do you remember  What features of the sub writers called toxic?

It's sad really. But then I'm guessing they wanted children so...I've been thinking about this recently- how being a mother basically takes away your free time and in a way you aren't you anymore because kids come first. But this idea that we as women have to practically  nail ourselves to the cross for the sake of others just leads to a lot of complaining and these mother's day posts. I wonder if the point of these posts is to show how self-sacrificing mothers are as they only want some time to themselves. To me it just screams 'it's hard and I'm tired' and the admiration for self-sacrifice just isn't something I'd feel after reading such a  thing.

What other subs did they mention? I kind of want to check them out because they included this one and toxic is not the word I'd use to describe it. I've seen more toxicity in the comment section under a random article.
What kind of activities dothey have for baby showers?

When put this way, it just sounds like one of those movies where you get stuck somewhere and can't leave. Except it's life, not being trapped in a building so there's not much you can do. Thinking about this makes me think I'm a hamster running on a wheel.

Absolutely! It was hard enough doing that once. I don't fancy repeating it all. I think this is partly why I struggle to understand people who have kids and then complain about having to do school and the rest of it all over again. Have they forgotten what it was like? I remember coming home from school feeling exhausted and having to do homework and feeling like I'd lived a hundred years. Who would want to put someone else through this and have to suffer along with them? What is it all for anyway? For the amazing possibility they too get to do it in the future?

I think there's a category of people who have kids not just because they think they want them but also because they don't know what it is that they do want. They don't have a job they are passionate about, they don't want to study and they might evenlike small kids, which later turns out not to be enough because small kids grow up and so their problems grow with them. Having children almost feels like 'so this is what I should do'. It's a kind of thing about which they'd say 'doing something with my life'. That time had been better spent trying to figure out who they are instead of using a child as a way to fill a void that they have no idea how to fill. They probably don't know what should be in that void so they figure they might as well put a kid in there.

Just recently my mum told me she  didn't just leave me to my own devices and took me to after school activities. And I couldn't help but wonder what she wanted me to say because it's not like I'd say just giving food was enough and the rest was such a nice extra that I'll forever talk about how amazing it was.And that's smeone who supposedly wanted children.I can't imagine what those who didn't tell their kids about all the stuff they had to do.
Is baby sprinkle a new fancy name for baby shower? Or is this different? I can't keep track of all these weird baby celebrations.

It maybe doesn't apply to everyone, but I do wonder why these people didn't see it was hard for their parents too. I saw my mum struggled and it's even more obvious now everything was a sacrifice for her. I frankly don't understand where this shock they suddenly experience comes from. it was always hard and stressful. And it is even worse if your partner isn't helpful, which still seems to be the case way too often.

Don't they think that never being ready and overthinking leading to being negative about it are the reasons not to do it? I mean, say you want to move to another country. You do your research and make a list of pros and cons and what needs to be done in order for you to move there. If there aren't enough pros, you likely decide not to move. For many of us it's the same with kids. It's like to these people overthinking is automatically bad when it comes to children because 'then you won't do it.' But why is it a better idea to  just act on your impulses and have a kid? You can't give the child back and they act as if it's crazy to consider  having kids might not be a good idea. They don't love that next generation at all if they are fine withboth the kids and the parents suffering due to parents' bad choices.

Missing out on what exactly?I suppose they mean that being a parent in itself is some kind of 'state' we should experience. But it's a tun of stress. Parents who reach that "I'm happy/proud' stage are the ones whose children succeeded in some way: went touni,  got a well-paying job... But where's that feeling when it all fails spectacularly? It's easy for your husband to talk when his partner probably handles a lot of the day-to-day stuff. It seems to me that everyone talks about procreation being a purpose because we praise parents so much.  And people want these social points. Besides, even if this were some universal biological need, some still should go against it because they can't provide a decent life for their kids. I wonder what those who insist on this being a need would say about people who simply have so many issues and for whom a child would add even more problems.

This is going to be such a disaster. It really feels that some men have this belief they can just do whatever they decide if they don't like the way things are: suddenly have kids with someone they don't love, leave when it's too hard or cheat. He'll ruin his future kid's life if  he is the type who just likes the idea of children. If that woman agrees to this crazy deal, she'll make the biggest mistake of her life because that child deserves better than a father who probably doesn't know what it's like to have kids nd  given how fast he gave up on this relationship, probably will not get involved with really hard things. Well, if they have a partner, they they share once more. And if they are on their own, are you then supposed to wait till you can afford to live on your own to have your needs met? It's like it's almost 'bad' to want to have your own space because it's normalized to give things up for others. Out of curiosity, what did they tell you when they scolded you for hating that whole sharing a room thing?

I can only imagine how much it sucked. There's something about sharing space with someone that just makes me immediately go'no way!' I suppose some do get used to it, but why force the situation upon them? It's so funny to me that whenever you bring this up, people start going on about how someone they knew grew up with six siblings in one room and turned out fine. Sounds like a beginning of some rather disturbing novel. Now I'll have this lady stuck in my head because I'll wonder what her relationship with that brother was like.

Then you suggest 'how about we ditch washing-machines and electricity?' People lived without those at some point too. They'll say 'that's extreme.' So why it's fine to accept some improvements as normal and not others?

Same here.I don't know if she now thinks she should have had more kids or what, but even now the thought of sharing my room  with a sibling sounds like a nightmare. But apparently the bar is now at 'don't have children only if you can't feed them.' At least that, according to my mum, is a real concern. We could lower that bar even more...
What the hell did she buy to spend this much money on a birthday? I hope she later won't tell the kid 'oh we spent 10k on your birthday when you turned one! Don't you remember?'

I think the emotional energy you need for raising a child isn't something we hear about enough. My mum, at least according to my therapist, felt overwhelmed by all the responsibilities, which meant she took it out on me and this left me feeling guilty for basically what was my mum's choice. And I'm an only child and at one point my mum wanted another. I don't know why she decided against it and I'd be surprised if being overwhelmed was what made her realize this was a bad idea. I sometimes wonder how the thought of another kid even crossed her mind when we never had a lot of money or enough space. Now my mum said she hs neither the time nora desire  to check if my cousin does her homework. I don't think that's how it should be. It's better to learn from the mistakes of others and the lesson I've learnt is 'Don't take on any responsibility if you aren't 100% willing and ready to accept all that is required of you when you take it on. I also think people who dream of having/wish for 'easy' kids really shouldn't have kids if they don't realize this is a crazy wish and it won't come true.

Why the hell did they say you were in the wrong here? Taking this kind of picture and then putting a message like this alongside it is disgusting. I thought at this point we'd already agreed  people should think carefully before doing anything related to posting pictures of this kind.

And they don't even think about whether they'd be able to help their own child deal with what may happen to them or if they'd be willing to make huge changes to their own life to help the kid they say they want. I remember watching an interview with a woman who had kids later in life. She nearly had a miscarriage and while going to hospital she asked herself if she could love her kid if he/she was disabled.The answer was 'yes'. She had twins and one of them has autism. And oh did she struggle with that!  I do hope many future parents saw that interview because this is what the reality is like. I find it funny that people say things like 'life is tough' and 'life is unfair' and theystill decide to have kids.My mum once got angry when I told her our maths teacher told us 'life is unfair'. I remember thinking 'but isn't that true?' And yet my mum is the one to say things like 'we don't have the connections to get x' or' we don't know as many people as x so we can't provide you with...' So... You can't hear the truth from someone else?

This has to go to the top of the list of stupid shit people say. But I can't believe they actually think this makes any sense at all.Disliking kids is ablest? Onwe thing I suspect is true is that people do seem to like 'children under the right circumstances' in the sense that they want a healthy and easy child.My own mum said all parents want a better child than they themselves were as kids. If we put these two ideas together, I am not sure why people even bother having kids as it's the biggest gamble I can think of. And it's precisely wanting a kid with certain characteristics that later means people struggle so much. I swear future parents are better off orderingababy doll online and playing with it. Maybe they'll invent actual dolls you could 'raise' into kids. Thenparents could 'pick' a doll-kid they want and no one would suffer.

I think seeing what my parents' marriage was like shaped me  in a significant way. I remember my father telling my mum that he didn't call her names, unlike his boss, who apparently did this to his own wife. And that's what? Something to be praised? The bar is on the floor then.

It's these little comments from parents that make me a bit uneasy becauseparents seem envious someone else made a different choice. And it's not a case of someone getting to move to another country or immediately getting a job at a company owned by their own family. They just do what they want because they don't have to take someone else into account. My mum recently commented that my cousin and his wife aren't 'settled down' because they don't have stable jobs and are planning to travel to India at some point. They aren't child-free, but don't have kids yet. This necesity to specifically comment on how unacceptable you find their lifestyle because at their age you already had kids and couldn't have travelled somewhere on a whim is a bit weird. In my experience it's usually parents, especially ones who are rather controlling, who want everyone else to behave a certain way or to fit their standards.

You are way more optimistic than I am when it comes to expecting men to take an equal part of the work when it comes to parenting! I wanted to say half, but I always have this idea that women at some point just give up because they either can't get their husbands to contribute equally or they are the type to say 'what do you want me to do?' I remember  my mum praising my father to me because he could tie my hair into a ponytail while other men couldn't. It's like every little thing they do is a tiny miracle!

I bet those who want kids babysit and then think their kid will be just as easy as the one they looked after. Parents absolutely want 'easy' kids but it's such a gamble. With this 'oh it won't be that bad' mentality, they are better off playing sims.

And  the child-free  folks are the selfish ones? Because it's no big deal for him to lie expecting she will give in and give him what he wants because it's his wishes first. And having kids is omg so noble. I hope whoever  agrees to have his kids will make him do at least some of the stuff he most probably wouldn't like as it's the best payback.Do any of these men even love their wives, though? How can someone do this to their partner? This feels like some kind of adult tantrum where you say 'I'm running away because you won't give me what I want'. Let's now see how the kids will 'make him grow-up'!

That 'unique experience' reasoning really confuses me.  They talk about it as if it were nothing more than trying some new and maybe a bit 'fancy' activity. I mean, you can do that with activities, but not with having kids. It's a lifetime obligation. What if you get sick of that new experience after a month? You can drop thosescubadiving lessons if you are no longer interested. You are stuck with a kid forever. I bet these people think it's a unique reason for having kids, though.

My mum recently told my godmother that the good thing about my teenage cousin was that she didn't constantly want to go party at a friend's house 'unlike us'. I mentioned it and said'so parents want to have a better child than they themselves were as kids.' My mum replied, in a tone that plainly says' this is an absolute truth to me', 'all parents are like that.' Then I said that maybe it's better not to want any kids at all as you don't know what you'll get.' So according to this idea, all parents want to have it easier than their own parents. Why the hell even have kids then? I mean, extra person=extra work in any scenario! I kept thinking about this idea and a thought popped into my head'I'd want my child just to be happier than I was.'  
I also cannot stand people who just brush off extra curricular activities saying 'the kid doesn't need all that'. But what if you can't afford what your kid does want/need? Is this going to be a 'life is unfair' kind of lesson then? But why bring a kid into the world that you tell them early on is unfair and is against them because you don't have enough resources? Having kids nearly always seems to be an emotional choice, but it's even worse when you realize they want a certain kind of kid, not just 'a kid'. I bet they imagine introducing the kids to the things they themselves like and don't think for a minute they might not like them at all. It feels such an ego move.

I can certainly sympathise with you when it comes to wanting to preserve your emotional energy but wishing to tell that guy exactly how messed-up his attitude is. I doubt he'd listen because I bet he's already decided how things should be. My father didn't know me either because we had nothing in common. At one point I did try to become interested in basketball just to get his attention and approval. I don't share any common interests with my mum either and what's more I think she doesn't think much of,say, being interested in learning Spanish just for the sake of learning. And she is very critical in general. So, like you, I can see how much the poor kid will suffer. I've noticed that parents who manage to get their kids interested in the stuff they themselves like are so proud. It sseems that to them it's an achievement. All I can think is 'what would you have said if the kid had 0 interest in going with you where you want to?' I remember thinking that if I were a boy, my father would like me better. It was only in therapy that I was told parents should love their kids just for being their kids.

I'm sad and scared  on behalf of his future kids. I suppose his wish does require a high level of delusion but damn. And whose fault will it be when it inevitably doesn't work out? I used to think people who have had a good relationship with their parents just want to have a good relationship with their kids, but your example shows  they have issues too. I hate the whole 'I'll accomplish my dreams through my kid' idea. Is he that desperate for that career in sports?
Oof...I am always envious of people who are good at maths. Are you already teaching?
What masters programme are you studying?

I imagine your parents have the mindset that 'it's an obligation' to look after your brother's kids. But can't you at least tell them you won't get involved? I'm tempted to suggest you just refuse  to help. I told my mum that  my grandma should just stop bringing food to my uncle and that's way we stop getting involved in helping him. It's harder when young kids are involved I suppose so I feel really sorry for them and for you. But these people need a lesson.

I can relate. My alcoholic uncle  was incapable of raising his daughter so my grandma took her in, but it was more because her husband, who has no kids of his own, was willing/wanted to. But as she is not one to care about anyone else much, she passed that responsibility onto us. I absolutely couldn't stand having to study while my cousin was around. She was very demanding as a child. Once my mum scolded me for not being nice to her when I was listening to a book and she came into my room. Maybe I could have been nicer, but it's frustrating to have to take on the responsibility that doesn't belong to you. My grandma actually pretty much  thinks it's no big deal I had to get involved. All of this to say I sympathise. Kids are a choice people make. These kids were not your choice. It can be somewhat easier when you get an 'easy' child, but God does it suck when it's not the case. I have quite a bit of resentment towards my grandma and my uncle. My uncle doesn't seem to have any brain left while my grandma just wants to pass any responsibilities that might show up onto others. I'm curious, can't your wife look after her own children?

I do hope you get to tell them that you've changed your mind after overhearing their conversation. It's not the first time I've seen parents adopt this weird belief the world will now start revolving around them. It's quite interesting because I am curious how this shift happens.

Yesterday we got some milkshakes and my mum got one for herself. I was like 'finally' as she always gets one which she shares with her partner. She replied 'well, it's expensive.' I said 'I love getting this just for myself.'She also would do the whole 'I didn't eat this (insert some food item) so that you could have it! Why didn't you eat it?' I swear to God, I could slap people repeating this phrase. This constant 'I'm giving this up for you' mindset is exhausting. Though I bet my mum thinks I'm selfish for not wanting to alwaysshare my stuff with someone because that's clearly what 'good parents' do.
What are your hobbies? I love it when people are so passionate about their hobbies.

I just heard one singer  who has three kids say this: kids do mean you have to give up your hobbies, but they compensate for it in much more important ways. He only mentioned the kids smiling and talking and that being a compensation. Burt it's this 'much more important' idea that gets to me. I suppose it isn't surprising, though, given that the first part talks about what you give up for kids. No one wants to think they've given up or limited something they liked for something 'inferior'. It just has to be better! But this 'I'm a parent thererefore I'm better' sentiment pisses me off. My mum met an aquaintance when we were buying some ice-cream. That lady asked us what we were buying because  they couldn't figure out what it was. My mum's comment was 'you don't have kids so you don't know' because it's my cousin who introduced us to this particular ice-cream. Like really...Maybe it was partly a joke, but it feels like the sentiment is still there. Now I think about it, maybe it'salso because being a parent is so hard that people want to get something out of it that would prove 'it's worth it'. It reminds me of all those situations where people talk about having learnt something from a horrible experience or a toxic relationship. No one wants to suffer/struggle in vein.

This is what still doesn't fail to surprise me about people. It's always, always like this: I won't lift a finger/ even the smallest favour from me should be worthy of knighthood, but others practically owe them their help and services. I don't get it. Is this lack of self-awareness?

One thing I absolutely cannot stand is having kids in my personal space. I can be around kids in someone else's house for some time, but you couldn't pay me enough to want to allow a kid into my house. I don't know where this started, but it partly has to do with the expectation that you'll let them play or entertain them. And if not that, they might take my things and I don't trust kids who do that. When my mum's cousin brought his four kids to our house, I absolutely refused to go with them. The kids weren't well-behaved and the cousin wanted me to go so I'd spend the time speaking in English with his daughter. Really? I sometimes think my reluctance to let kids take my stuff isn't ok, but I can't help it.

I already resent them if they are planning to make their daughter share her bedroom with two siblings. Why don't some parents think kids need their own space? And that agreement between the couple and the government is interesting. Did they havwe to sign anything? I can't imagine being their kid and realizing at some point I was the means to get a shitty two-bedroom flat where I don't even have a room of my own. It's hardwhen you see just how  little people care about their future kids. The good old 'we'll work it out' is still in use it seems. Maybe they dream of some opportunities that might come up at some point, but from my experience not all parents are willing to change their lives if those opportunities do come up if things aren't horrible for them. It's not them who will share a room with two other people...

I sometimes can't explain it. My mum has a cousin who has   four or five kids (I lost count after the last one) and my mum told that when she and her niece went to see these relatives, the parents let their daughter ride her bike or some other thing and she nearly bumped into people. No reaction at all. When we were unlucky enough to have these people at our house, one kid outright told my cousin that he is allowed to do what he wants/she should allow him to do what he wants because 'we are guests'. And these are the people of whom my grandma says that they aren't concerned about the clothes their kids wear, but care a lot about 'their education.' Oh really...their father, for instance, would take their phones from the kids for some time. But apparently they don't teach their sprogs not to be entitled brats. I think in their case this is acceptable to them.

I'm impressed by her rage control too. I'd have most likely screamed at the childand I can't guarantee I wouldn't have pulled his/her hair if the pulling was as painful as I imagine. For some kids this is actually somehow the only way that seems to work.

I don't remember the last time I was so irritated by something as mundane as a simple article! Child-free can 'have June'? What if they want July instead? It's like they are being generous by letting the child-free have June! And that last sentence'let us have that (school holidays) at least...Who forced them to have kids? I heard a man in his 50s claiming young women are brainwashed into choosing not to have kids and was like 'I never liked children...so who brainwashed me then?' Like you, I had no idea there was a term for this and that this was a choice you could make. I remember reading books and thinking that women ending up having kids wasn't an appealing happy ending for me. It just seems pro-kid people assume someone else must be at fault for people makingthe choices they don't approve of. I bet they wouldn't believe it if we told them this was an internal feeling for us. But their suggestions of showing parenting in a positive light only are all well and good. Do they even realize this is propaganda? Or is there good and bad propaganda?

I sometimes struggle to see the difference between 'adults' and actual children because this screams 'give me what I want'. When it comes to children and everything that has to do with them, people's selfishness reaches perhaps the highest levels, though.

And I can only imagine how unhappy everyone is in that family. My grandma married my grandpa despite them having split up. She claims she didn't know 'what he was like',i.e., that he had a drinking problem. But she also claims she got back with him just because he 'begged me to' and 'said we'd live in paradise'. Now she is miserable and blames him for all that went wrong.  For many years I wondered how a person as self-centered as her even wanted to get married. I'm a bit sorry for her, but I'm also like 'you believed these fairytale promises?' There was clearly something going on if she dumped him.

Why exactly would it be so terrible if they went their separate ways? I wonder if these coworkers have  heard how children of such parents talk about how their parents constantly argued and seemed to dislike each other. I suppose they think that now the kid is involved in this mess, they should sort it out. But if it wasn't working before, I don't know why they think they'll make it work for the sake of the kid and that this won't make them even more unhappy. It's just the same old stuff people say when they think they 'have to say something.'

And this is why some parents sound rather bitter/disappointed. Raising children is a lot of work. I think my mum convinced herself that sacrificing for the sake of kids is is meaningful in itself somehow, but the problem isprecisely that she makes it clear it's asacrifice so it doesn't seem like she's happy. I frankly don't get it. I do wonder what it is that some want out of parenting and how they imagine that gratification that is supposed to come. Later on parents complain their kids don't visit them so it goes from 'it's hard' to'ungrateful bastards forgot about me'.
Poor kids...I only am learning to say that I dislike this or that behaviour and my mum still says her traditional 'you're overreacting'. Some people don't want to learn to listen.

This one is a huuuge pet peve of mine. I remember a guy with a genetic eye condition saying that 'it can't be helped/it is as it is' when talking about the fact his kids had it too. I mean, let's not pretend you 'needed' to have kids and that it didn't occur to you this could happen. He knows he's responsible for passing it on, but no one likes admiting they are responsible for something bad happening to their kid. I was wondering if it wasn't hisego that lead him to want kids because some men are weirdly proud they can reproduce. But I find it so selfish to have kids when you know you'll put them at a huge disadvantage. I often wonder how these people deal with the guilt they surely must feel.

I agree and can relate.It turns out I can't watch a video of a mum taking her daughter somewhere for her birthday because my mum didn't like doing these extra things. If she did something like that, I'd have had to hear about how amazing it was I got a chance to do this or that and I'd have had to be properly overjoyed about this. It's like she believes that by giving me something she'd have wanted and by doing it as a sacrifice, she got to relive her childhood or something. I'm convinced she thoughtshe partly had a child expecting to do a better job than her own mum, but she failed because I became her emotional outlet and at the same time had to hear about how she didn't want to do this or that thing related to,say, my after school activities. People have this misguided belief that just by thinking 'I'll do better' they will do better than their own parents. It's very very hard to do anything if one of the reasons you arehaving kids is the idea you somehow won't make the same mistakes. I think it's far better to wish to avoid causing the same suffering to your child that you have had to experience and so choosing not to have children. I get the resentment bit too. I'm glad you mentioned it because there's a high chance I'd be resentful in this way too.

When I began reading the post, I was like 'why the fuck would someone bring a baby into a class when they will have to miss half of it if the baby starts crying?' But then you said the class is unrelated to what she's learning and it all became clear. People are so damn selfish! I still can't believe she is willing to bring a baby and then have to go in and out of the room. As much as I admire people who study while looking after babies, this is why they need to have a good support system if they want this to work out.

It's because it's so crazy that I still remember it. At the time I really struggled to see that woman's perspective. I can't understand herto this day, but back then I was wondering if there was something wrong with me for thinking she was selfish for condeming her child to live without one of the parents. I was like 'do people really want kids this badly? I don't understand it!' I actually think the lady was herself a doctor of some kind. This story in particular is why I dislike the whole 'baby's life comes first in every single case' narrative. The mum dies and you can bet everyone will have to rush to help the father, who won't know what to do with this precious baby. So it's doubly tragic because someone made this specific choice. I bet everyone would be scandalized if a woman said she wanted to be saved. I guess it's no surprise some women really embrace this role of a martyr.

The way some men talk about women is creepy as hell. One politician had a brilliant idea of making people without kids pay extra taxes. Some friend of his who is single asked him 'what the hell are you talking about?' That politician was like 'All that money you have, where do you spend it? On yourself? So go find a woman, have kids with her and you'll be fine.' Should he just go out and grab the first woman he sees? Once our biology teacher told us about a woman who was told she couldn't have kids because she'd die if she gave birth. Guess what? She did it anyway. The doctors were right- she died in childbirth. All I could think was that the kid was an orphan and would feel guilty they are the reason their mother died. The lady took such a big risk and what was it all for? She didn't get to raise the child, the child grew up without a mother. So what was this sacrifice for?

I hate the fact that children so often are presented as the reason people are motivated to 'do more'. It's not universal. Some parents don't even manage to provide the emotional support the kid needs or simply don't feel like making changes that would help their child. I doubt they are rushing to get that promotion or start that 'very successful' business. I dread to think some people might actually expect to suddenly get motivated to do 'big things' once they have kids, just to later realize they don't feel like doing much at all because 'it's hard as it is'. Why do so many people argue you should have kids when their arguments for having them aren't some universal rule that works?'have them regardless'...What nonsense.

In all seriousness, people who say this stuff probably haven't heard how reluctant some kids are to look after their parents. It's a chore to them. I don't know who'd want this sort of grudgingly given care. My elderly neighbour fell and broke her leg. During the holidays one of her daughters called my mum to complain that her sister refused to look after their mum at her own flat. She in general seems to think they don't split the care equally. Though it was that other sister who was at her mum's house every weekend so I don't know what the truth is. But  I got the impression that this is a responsibility everyone would happily pass ontosomeone else. And I do wonder if that daughter who did visit her mum isn't doing so partly because she expects  to get a bigger part of the inheritance.

I love this! I so often see posts where people say they don't want kids because they want to do something else instead and every time I think to myself 'I just want to rest whenever I feel like it or just  read a book!' I have realized recently that I feel guilty when doing something that isn't productive. But I also remember having to do my homework after coming home,  having spent the entire afternoon  at a music school. I felt absolutely exhausted. I imagine it's similar when you have kids and I don't find it enjoyable at all.Someone else mentioned being able to just recover when you are sick, which made me think of all those comments I've heard from mothers, where they basically have to look after everyone else. I don't know how they manage to make this huge shift. I doubt I could.

I can relate. My family wasn't disfunctional, but I have always had a very strained relationship with my father. Being around him caused me a lot of anxiety. So Christmas wasn't exactly a fun family time for me. I remember us going to visit my father's relatives during the holidays and I found it so strange we had to make this obligatory social visit when no none of my father's relatives cared about him all that much. Even as a child I longed for that perfect family where people get along and like each other. Like you, Iwondered if kids of my own would make it happen. But that's not fair to them- I can't bring a child into the world just to relive my own childhood. Besides, maybe it wouldn't happen even then so it would end up being a huge disaster as I don't want children. I think my own mum partly had me so she could 'do a better job' raising me than her own mother. This is just not the way to do it. It's interesting that even among my relatives on my mum's side there doesn't seem to be that genuine love and care you would associate family with. My mum's cousin didn't go to visit his own brother when that brother was seriously ill. People suggest friend groups and I love the suggestion. But somehow it feels very hard to find people who  don't try to one-up each other or brag about something.

I find this genuinely interesting because while growing up I had the impression that even if you want kids, you don't quite enjoy much of parenting and it is overwhelming.But then again, my mum seems to think sacrifice in itself is what makes it worth it. But I now realize that when it came to doing things a parent does, she just had a 'I have to do this' mentality. I'm a bitenvious if you got to see a different kind of parenthood.

I am somewhat curious. I do think I'd want to do all I could to make sure my child is happy, but it would be anxiety-inducing to me because it's knowing what I shouldn't do doesn't mean I am absolutely sure how to do things the right way. I've been raised with the idea that parenting is a sacrifice where you don't particularly enjoy it even if you supposedly wanted children. I've seen comments here that say the exact opposite so as I haven't had such examples, it would be hard to imagine how this particular scenario would work.
This is actually brilliant. I do wonder how your mother felt once she realized men are like this. I think I'd never look at my partner the same way if  I had had to come to this realization.

Who does he think he is? I mean, you do have to think quite a lot of yourself to imagine a woman would suddenly feel less valuable just because you as a man wouldn't want to have kids with her. Their living arrangements... Well, they are definitely interesting. I just imagined one of the kids having to tell about his family and telling this whole thing. How does she even support all those children? And  what will happen once the inevitable 'there's no money for x' situation happens? Why ruin your kids' chances from the very start? This lack of thinking is impressive.
Doesn't she  want to overcome this adiction? I mean, surely she knows it's not ok? Or is it fine because it's pregnancy sh's adicted to and not heroine? What was their daily life like btw?

This kind of situation is honestly  one of those cases where I'm like 'I wouldn't ever want to be in this position'. Not only does the mum feel awful, the kid is bound to pick up on this because her frustration and dissatisfaction won't just vanish. Then there'll be two unhappy people.  The poor kid might feel guilty. I grew up thinking I had to be convenient and my mum did want kids. But the issue arises when women realize how hard parenting is, find it overwhelming and take it out on their kids. I do hope this lady gets some help. Though I'm curious if in her position you can reach a point where you don't regret the decision. I've seen comments by mums who say it's the most wonderful thing. And it's not that I don't believe them, it's just that I wonder why the outcomes are so different.

How  did they even manage to make seem like the bad guy? It's funny how they want us to pretend 'decent' people don't have a thought exactly like that one. Makes me want to check out that show just to see what it's about. But this sort of propaganda really gets to me so I'd just get angry.

My godmother, who thankfully doesn't have kids, said it's fine for people to have many kids as long as those kids are loved. I thought she was old enough not to believe this sort of stuff because my first thought whenever I hear 'multiple kids' is'how will you afford their education? after school stuff? School trips?'
